title: OIDC Pushed Authorization Requests (PAR)
subtitle: Push the whole authorization request over a secure back channel first, then redirect with just a short-lived request_uri — so the parameters never touch the browser URL (RFC 9126).

steps.label: Start sign-in
steps.lede: The user begins sign-in. The client builds the full authorization request locally: a PKCE code_verifier and S256 challenge, state, nonce, and scope.
steps.devtools: Nothing on the wire yet. Everything the browser would normally carry on the /authorize URL is about to be sent on the back channel instead.

steps.label: POST /par
steps.lede: The client pushes the COMPLETE authorization request to the PAR endpoint, authenticating with its client credentials. Every parameter travels here, server-to-server — none of it will touch the browser.
steps.devtools: Not in the browser — read client server logs or AS logs on the /par path. The Basic value decodes to s6BhdRkqt3:cli-s3cr3t-shhh. Every authorization parameter is in this body; client-auth failure returns 401 invalid_client.

steps.label: 201 request_uri
steps.lede: The AS validates and stores the request, then returns an opaque, single-use request_uri handle with a short TTL. The client must redirect before it lapses.
steps.devtools: request_uri is a one-time reference to the stored request — the only authorization detail that will appear in the browser. expires_in (60s) is short; a stale or reused handle gets invalid_request_uri at /authorize.

steps.label: Redirect to /authorize (request_uri only)
steps.lede: The browser is redirected to the authorization endpoint carrying ONLY client_id and request_uri. The long parameters are absent from the URL — that is PAR working.
steps.devtools: This is the request to inspect in DevTools. Confirm the query string holds only client_id and request_uri — no scope, redirect_uri, code_challenge, state, or nonce. The AS resolves request_uri to the stored request and ignores any extra query params. A plain /authorize with no request_uri, when the AS requires PAR, is rejected with invalid_request.

steps.label: Redirect back with code
steps.lede: After the user logs in and consents, the AS 302-redirects back to redirect_uri with a single-use authorization code and the echoed state.
steps.devtools: Find the 302 whose Location points at your redirect_uri. Verify the returned state equals the af0ifjsldkj you pushed in step 2 — a mismatch means CSRF; abort.

steps.label: POST /token (redeem code)
steps.lede: The client exchanges the code plus the original PKCE code_verifier for tokens. The AS recomputes S256(code_verifier) and matches it to the challenge that was pushed in step 2.
steps.devtools: Back-channel, not in the browser. The code_verifier dBjftJeZ… proves the same client that pushed the request is redeeming the code: its S256 hash must equal the code_challenge pushed in step 2, binding the whole flow together.
